purpose: Deepen STANDARDIZATION_BEFORE_ROUTING and COMPATIBILITY_WEIGHTED_DENSITY. Apparently similar demand is not economically aggregatable unless the conversion cost between task variants and a common capability/acceptance interface is low enough. This scan treats changeover, protocol translation, qualification scope, tooling and standards as exchange friction, not as a new ontology.

evidence: Dongxing Xuzhou factory operates automated lines with minute-level rapid changeover for multi-variety, small-batch production.
The factory uses integrated scheduling, sensing and automated control rather than assuming different product variants are naturally interchangeable.
findings.interpretation: Small batches become aggregatable on one production system only after setup/changeover cost is engineered downward. Free nominal capacity without low conversion cost would not be equally callable.

evidence: A Jiangsu advanced intelligent-factory case uses modular workstation design, standardized process modules and rapid reconfiguration for high-mix low-volume production.
A related factory case reports scan-based changeover shortened to about three minutes and explicitly identifies inconsistent equipment communication protocols as an implementation obstacle.
findings.interpretation: Compatibility is engineered through modularity, common interfaces and standardized process state. Protocol mismatch is the inverse case: capacity can exist but remain non-composable.

evidence: Jiangsu Medical Device Testing Institute's 2026 CNAS/CMA review evaluated specific added testing items/parameters; the institute expected 278 new parameters and about 2,491 total parameters after approval.
Testing capability is therefore parameter/method/scope specific rather than equivalent to generic laboratory availability.
findings.interpretation: A nearby laboratory with spare time is not automatically compatible with a task. Legal qualification, method, instrument range and accepted standard are part of task compatibility.

evidence: A Changzhou testing/verification organization covers Chinese, European, US and Japanese vehicle/charging standards and offers a one-test/multi-market pathway.
Public reporting says local firms can avoid sending products overseas for repeated certification and can save more than RMB 2 million per certification case.
findings.interpretation: The underlying product may be identical, but different market standards fragment the acceptance interface. A trusted translation/testing layer converts one technical artifact into multiple accepted representations and thereby expands callability.

evidence: A Xuzhou engineering-machinery supplier expanded from roughly a dozen standard cylinder products to more than 200 variants and invested in production-line modification to support rapid switching for small-batch, multi-variety orders.
The change was described as necessary to keep pace with downstream flexible demand.
findings.interpretation: Downstream variety propagates compatibility cost upstream. Shared or routed capacity remains viable only if variant-switch cost does not overwhelm the value of smaller orders.

evidence: Earlier shared transport, laboratory, waste and expert-routing examples likewise require compatible time, material or task representations.
findings.interpretation: Raw demand density should be discounted by the cost of converting each variant into the common execution and acceptance coordinates of the shared node.

search_rules_refined.name: COMPATIBILITY_CONVERSION_COST
questions: What must change before task B can use the same capability as task A?
How much time, tooling, qualification, setup, cleaning, translation, calibration, data mapping or retraining is required?
Does this conversion cost scale per task, per batch or once per interface?
After including conversion cost, does aggregation still create positive surplus?
search_rules_refined.relationship_to_existing_doctrine: Deepening of STANDARDIZATION_BEFORE_ROUTING and COMPATIBILITY_WEIGHTED_DENSITY; not a new top-level ontology.

search_rules_refined.name: COMMON_EXECUTION_AND_ACCEPTANCE_COORDINATES
questions: Can different tasks be represented using the same process/specification fields?
Can the same capability execute them without excessive reconfiguration?
Can the receiver accept outputs under a common or translatable evidence standard?

search_rules_refined.name: CHANGEOVER_COST_AS_DENSITY_DISCOUNT
search_rules_refined.pattern: apparent recurring volume - setup/changeover/translation/qualification burden = economically routable volume
search_rules_refined.boundary: This is a qualitative search heuristic, not a numerical scoring formula.
